834: (16) It is permitted to place an infanda (a type of pastry) opposite the fire in a place where the hand is scalded, even though the fat within it that was congealed returns and melts. {Rama: And all the more so a pot that has congealed sauce — when the fat melts it is no longer visible — which is permitted (Rabbeinu Yeruham part 3). And some are stringent (Ran chapter 29). And the custom is to be stringent. However in a case of need one may rely on the first opinion.}
837: (20) 'In a place where it is yad soledes bo' — the Beit Yosef brings that the Mordechai wrote like the Baal HaTerumah — which is the stringent view here — and Rabbeinu Yechiel of Paris brought proof to permit from the chapter Kira. It is still good to be careful not to place it so close to the fire that it will be yad soledes bo.
839: (21) 'And even though the fat is, etc.' — this is the opinion of the Semag: one should not forbid on account of nolad, and it is comparable to the ruling that one may not crush snow or hail as written in siman 320 seif 11, for here he does nothing with his hands but rather it melts on its own.
841: (40) 'In a place where it is yad soledes bo' — the Levush writes that it should read 'in a place where it is not yad soledes bo.' But it appears to me that here since it was already cooked and it is a dry item there is no cooking after cooking.
843: (41) 'And all the more so a pot that has, etc., which is permitted' — but nevertheless it is forbidden because of cooking for those who are stringent as written in seif 15.
845: (36) 'Yad soledes bo' — the Levush writes that where it cannot reach yad soledes bo there is no concern for cooking. But it appears to me that here since it was already cooked and is dry there is no concern of cooking.
847: (37) 'And it melts' — for he does not perform any melacha with his hands, but it melts on its own.
849: (38) 'Permitted' — but nevertheless it is forbidden for cooking purposes for those who are stringent, as written in seif 15.
851: (50) 'Seif 16, permitted' — and it is not comparable to the melting of snow and hail explained later in siman 320 seif 9 which is forbidden because of nolad, for here the fat was thick and returns to being fat, and there is no nolad.
853: (51) 'And all the more so a pot' — for even according to Rashi — because it is nolad — it is permitted, as stated there 'but he gives, etc.'
855: (52) 'And some are stringent' — this follows the view that even in the pot one should be stringent because the fat floats visibly.
857: (7) 'And some are stricter' — see the Beer Heitev and see siman 84 which disagrees with the Magen Avraham and holds that even in a place where it is yad soledes bo there is no prohibition b'dieved.
859: (100) 'Infanda, etc.' — it is a pastry mentioned in several places, a double pastry filled with pieces of fat. One places it there in order to heat it. And the reason it is permitted is since it was already cooked and it is a dry item there is no cooking after cooking.
861: (101) 'Opposite the fire' — meaning on top of some intervening vessel, otherwise it is forbidden as stated above in siman 253 seif 3 and seif 5.
863: (102) 'And even though, etc.' — this is not comparable to crushing snow and hail explained later in siman 320, which is forbidden because of nolad — producing water — whereas here it was thick fat and returns to being fat.
865: (103) 'And all the more so a pot, etc.' — for when it melts the fat mixes with the sauce and is not noticeable, and this is truly comparable to what we say 'but he gives into the cup' because it is impossible to see it.
867: (104) 'Permitted' — meaning only regarding the prohibition of nolad it does not apply here; but regarding the prohibition of cooking, here it is stricter since the sauce is a wet item, and a wet item that cooled is subject to cooking after cooking.
869: (105) 'And some are stringent' — he holds that nolad also applies here, even in a pot where the fat is mixed with the sauce.
871: (106) 'To be stringent' — but before the oven is fired up it is permitted to place the pastry, since there are those who permit even afterward; and one should not do so in the presence of an ignoramus.
873: (107) 'In a case of need, one may rely' — meaning that then even l'chatchila it is permitted, and b'dieved in all cases one should not forbid.
875: (95) 'Infanda' — like our kind of bourekas, a pastry filled with meat or cheese. The essential point for this seif is that it contains fat.
877: (96) 'In a place where the hand is scalded' — and this is how it is heated, since there is no cooking after cooking. And even though the fat within it thereby becomes liquid, here the fat was not liquid before and is not considered a broth dish.
879: (97) 'Returns and melts' — we already saw that it is not forbidden to place it opposite the fire, and they were not concerned that it appears as if he is cooking. The Mechaber's view is that one need not be concerned about creating a new substance when the fat melts.
881: (98) 'Permitted' — the Rama refers to the method of the rishonim who forbid melting on account of creating a new substance, and writes that even according to them it is permitted to melt fat in a pot that has sauce, since when it melts it mixes with the sauce and is no longer visible.
883: (99) 'And some are stringent' — because it produces the fat.
885: (100) 'The first opinion' — the Rama decides that from the primary law it is permitted, but it is good l'chatchila to be stringent. And the Mechaber was not concerned about this stringency at all.
